open_points.subject: StaffAccount email-verification state after recovery override
open_points.text: R0-23 says "A staff account's email is its login identifier only" and that the portal has "no email verification", while R0-20 says the recovery override replaces the login email and "marks it verified".
open_points.question: Does StaffAccount retain any email-verification fact after email verification was removed, and precisely what state does "marks it verified" change during a recovery override?
options: Remove the verification effect; recovery atomically replaces only the login email and writes its audit record.
Retain a legacy email-verified fact that recovery sets, although authentication ignores it.
Interpret "verified" as a change to an account lifecycle status such as active.
open_points.default_guess: Remove the email-verification fact and treat the remaining "marks it verified" wording as obsolete, while preserving the email replacement and atomic audit.

witness.initial: An active staff account uses old@example.test as its login email.
events: An administrator performs the exceptional recovery override with new@example.test.
The portal commits the replacement and staff.recovery_override audit record.
outcomes: The account stores only new@example.test as its login identifier and has no verification state.
The account additionally stores a verified state for new@example.test, despite email otherwise being identifier-only.
witness.observer: A later domain/persistence implementer, and any administrator or operator inspecting the stored account state

open_points.subject: Agent access through cabinet_kernel
open_points.text: R0-23 explains that "the owner opens portal sessions himself and an agent works through cabinet_kernel", but cabinet_kernel is not defined as an external boundary or principal, ServicePrincipal capabilities are import-only, and the product supports exactly three principal types.
open_points.question: Is the cabinet_kernel sentence normative product behavior, and if so, whose credential or session authenticates the agent's requests, where is that trust boundary, and which actor is recorded in audit?
options: cabinet_kernel is outside the product and uses the owner's StaffAccount session, so every agent action is authorized and audited as the owner.
The agent has its own StaffAccount and session, even though the owner is said to open the sessions.
cabinet_kernel authenticates as a ServicePrincipal, requiring capabilities beyond the stated import-only set.
The sentence is explanatory only; cabinet_kernel and agent operation are not part of the specified product behavior.
open_points.default_guess: Treat cabinet_kernel as non-normative context and model no additional actor or boundary; only requests authenticated under one of the three specified principals exist.

witness.initial: The owner has an active administrator StaffAccount and has opened a portal session; an expense needs correction.
events: An agent instructs cabinet_kernel to submit the expense correction.
cabinet_kernel sends a request to the portal.
outcomes: The request uses the owner's session, succeeds, and the audit record identifies the owner with no agent provenance.
The request is rejected because cabinet_kernel or the agent has no defined portal principal or authorized credential.
witness.observer: The owner reviewing the result and an auditor reviewing actor provenance
